title: Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services

reading.body:
This incident shows AI-generated impersonation deployed at scale on social media platforms to commit fraud. Scammers used AI-generated images and videos of a real immigration attorney to create thousands of fake profiles across TikTok, Facebook, and Instagram, then directed victims to WhatsApp to solicit payments for fraudulent legal services. The deployment succeeded because social media platforms did not catch the impersonation before thousands of profiles accumulated and victims had already sent money.

The failure occurred at the point where platforms received uploaded content. Detecting this would have required either human review of profiles claiming professional credentials, automated systems to flag AI-generated imagery, or verification of identity before allowing someone to represent themselves as a licensed professional online. It is not established how the scammers generated the initial synthetic media, whether platforms were notified before the anti-piracy company intervened, or what mechanisms exist to prevent similar schemes.

reports.title: Scammers steal identity of renowned Miami attorney to target immigrants on social media
South Florida immigration attorney says AI scammers are using his identity to target immigrants
Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services
Legal resident loses thousands seeking citizenship to AI immigration attorney

summary:
Angel Leal, a South Florida immigration attorney with over 30 years of experience, has become the target of artificial intelligence scammers who are using fake videos and social media profiles featuring his likeness to defraud vulnerable immigrants. The criminals use AI-generated images and videos to promote fake immigration services, offering services like US residency assistance for payments of thousands of dollars. Leal discovered the scheme when potential clients began calling his office, and he learned the problem has significantly worsened over the past three months. An anti-piracy company hired by his firm has removed nearly 6,500 fake profiles across social media platforms, including 3,500 on TikTok, 2,400 on Facebook, and 544 on Instagram.

The scammers typically lure victims through social media videos that direct people to contact a WhatsApp number, where they exchange fake contracts and request payments through apps like Venmo, Zelle, and Cash App. Leal is warning immigrants to watch for these red flags and verify the identity of anyone offering legal services online. He emphasizes that his office never requests payments over the phone. The attorney plans to contact local and federal authorities this week to launch an investigation into the origin of the scams.
